solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Big hit as wrecking ball taken to flats? (11)

blocks.note: read literally: a thing that breaks up an apartment building

annotation.surface: A demolition crew swinging a wrecking ball into an apartment block, hailed as a big hit.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading; flats here are apartments, and a block of them is what gets busted.
annotation.definitionFit: Originally a wartime bomb able to flatten a whole city block, the word moved on to mean any huge commercial success.

entries.clue: Epsom Derby? (6)

blocks.note: the surface wants the Surrey racecourse; the setter uses it to mean English, as opposed to American
the surface wants the famous horse race; the setter means the American name for a round, hard felt hat

annotation.surface: A two-word reference to the famous English horse race.
annotation.walkthrough: The Derby is a flat race run at Epsom in Surrey. But Americans call the round hard hat a derby, and the English name for that same hat is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional-use definition: the hat called a derby in America is a bowler in England.

entries.clue: Viva the dental check! (4,11)

blocks.note: short for viva voce, a spoken exam, especially for a doctorate
the dentist's look inside the mouth

annotation.surface: A cheer for a trip to the dentist, as if a check-up deserved celebrating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Viva' looks like the Italian cheer; here it is the academic viva voce, an exam taken by speaking.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a viva is examined by speech, and a dental check examines the mouth, both meanings of oral.

entries.clue: Instrument contained spirit (10)

blocks.note: kettling is the police tactic of containing a crowd in a cordon

annotation.surface: A musical instrument that holds some kind of spirit inside it.
annotation.walkthrough: To kettle protesters is to hem them in, a term from British policing, which is why 'contained' is a past-tense verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the kettledrum, or timpani, is a percussion instrument shaped like a cauldron.

entries.clue: State where odd bits lost in dust-bath (4)

indicatorNotes.odd bits lost: the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh, are thrown away, and the even ones remain

blocks.note: d-U-s-T-b-A-t-H: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

annotation.surface: A place where a bird's dust-bath has lost some bits.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen does not count as a letter; count only the eight letters of dust and bath.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Utah is one of the fifty US states.

entries.clue: Fruity CEO? (3,6)

blocks.note: the surface wants an eccentric, colourful personality; the setter means a name made of fruit
the chief executive, the most senior person in a company

annotation.surface: A company chief with a colourful, perhaps eccentric, personality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests a lively character, but the setter wants the slang phrase for a boss that happens to contain a fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the slang for the most important person in an organisation is literally the highest fruit in the bunch.

entries.clue: Scarlet concealer applied to fibre in makeover (7)

indicatorNotes.concealer applied to: a concealer hides what it is put on, so RED covers and hides the fibre inside itself

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red

annotation.surface: A cosmetics tip: scarlet concealer dabbed on as part of a makeover.
annotation.walkthrough: Concealer is a makeup product, which suits 'makeover', but here the scarlet word itself does the concealing.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym from marketing: giving a company a new name and look is a makeover of its image.

entries.clue: Worker of wizardry perhaps in test of lexicographical knowledge? (8,3)

blocks.note: casting spells is one kind of wizardry, hence 'perhaps'
a worker is a type of bee in the hive

annotation.surface: A magician's assistant taking part in a word quiz.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue order is reversed: the worker comes first in the clue but last in the answer, as 'worker of wizardry' describes a bee that does magic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the contest tests how well competitors can spell words, knowledge of the dictionary.

entries.clue: Coastline that’s rocky in parts (9)

indicatorNotes.rocky: rocky also means unsteady, so the letters wobble out of their order

annotation.surface: A shore that is rocky only in some stretches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' fits a coastline so naturally that it hides its job as the rearranging signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something sectional is made of, or divided into, separate sections.

entries.clue: Primitive — as an aristocrat? (5)

blocks.note: from the first stage of development
an invented adjective: a peer's title plus -Y, the way 'lordly' means like a lord

annotation.surface: A jibe that aristocrats are primitive.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark licenses the made-up word: EARL-Y, behaving like an earl.
annotation.definitionFit: Primitive means belonging to an early stage; the second sense is a pun on the title earl.

entries.clue: Crumb also coloured red (9)

indicatorNotes.coloured: to colour a story is to distort it, so the letters are distorted into a new order

annotation.surface: A crumb that has also been dyed red.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red' reads as the colour of the crumb, but it is a noun here: a red wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Lambrusco is a sparkling Italian wine, usually red.

entries.clue: American author, one with French post? (6,6)

blocks.note: a Norman comes from Normandy in France
turns 'post' into a person: someone who deals in the post
to post is to mail, and one who does it is a mailer

annotation.surface: An American writer who takes up a job in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One with French post' reads as a diplomat abroad; split it, and it is a man from Normandy who sends letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Norman Mailer was an American novelist, author of The Naked and the Dead.

entries.clue: Good French drinking wine that’s fortified (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the phrase describes a thing (a place that's fortified), so it matches the noun

indicatorNotes.drinking: someone drinking takes a liquid inside, so BON takes the wine inside itself

blocks.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

annotation.surface: A fine French tipple that has been fortified, like port or sherry.
annotation.walkthrough: Fortified wine is a real thing, which hides that 'that's fortified' is the definition, a place rather than a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a bastion is a projecting part of a fortress, and by extension any stronghold.

entries.clue: Perfume, rotten odour ultimately, time for incense (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the end letter of each word

blocks.note: perfumE, rotteN, odouR: the last letters
an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A complaint about perfume that smells rotten, burning time as if it were incense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the scented stick, fitting perfume and odour; it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, meaning to anger.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once the verb sense is seen: to incense someone is to make them furious.

entries.clue: Wild West lawman, a petty war criminal (5,4)

indicatorNotes.criminal: a criminal breaks the rules, so the letters break out of their order

annotation.surface: A frontier sheriff dismissed as a small-time war criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'War criminal' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'criminal' is the signal acting on 'a petty war'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Wyatt Earp was a lawman of the Old West, famous for the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

entries.clue: Glue-stiffened cloth two males stuck together (7)

indicatorNotes.stuck together: things stuck together are joined, so the two animal words are set end to end

blocks.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: Two men stuck to each other by glue-stiffened fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Males' means male animals, not men; 'stuck' echoes the glue of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: buckram is coarse cloth stiffened with glue or size, used in bookbinding and hat-making.

entries.clue: This part of stair is erect (5)

annotation.definition: This part of stair is erect

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is only a part of the letters that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the last letter of stair, all of 'is', and the first two of erect

annotation.surface: A note on how stairs are built: this piece stands upright.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: of a step's two faces, the tread is flat and the answer is the upright one.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: the vertical board between two treads of a staircase is the part of the stair that stands erect.

entries.clue: Fairly new parts Waugh cut? (6)

indicatorNotes.parts: to part something is to split it, so the name is split open and N goes between its parts
indicatorNotes.cut: a cut name is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: Evelyn Waugh, the English novelist, stands for his first name
the first name without its last letter

annotation.surface: Asking whether Waugh's new book was cut fairly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waugh' stands for his first name, not the surname, which is the step most solvers miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to share evenly is to share fairly, with equal portions.

entries.clue: Wisdom built up legendary area? (8)

blocks.note: a saga is a legendary tale, used here as an adjective
a city is a built-up area; 'legendary' sits inside the phrase

annotation.surface: Wisdom accumulated over time in some fabled region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Built up' seems to go with wisdom, but it belongs to 'area', so the whole reads as a legendary built-up area.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sagacity is shrewd, practical wisdom.

entries.clue: University lecture (7)

blocks.note: a university in the English town of that name, west of London
a formal talk or recital; the French word lecture has the same sense

annotation.surface: A university lecture, seen from a student's timetable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'University' is a proper name here: Reading is a Berkshire town with its own university.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a place name standing for its university, and a public recital or lecture.

entries.clue: Stirrer got raita mixed up (8)

indicatorNotes.mixed up: like a stirred dip, the letters are mixed into a new order

annotation.surface: A kitchen spoon that has got the raita all mixed up.
annotation.walkthrough: Raita is an Indian yoghurt dip, so 'stirrer' reads as a spoon; it is a troublemaker.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the British sense: a stirrer is someone who stirs up trouble.

entries.clue: I’m annoyed about people behind Polish national song (3,4,3,10)

indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to face the other way, so the exclamation is read backwards
indicatorNotes.behind: the people stand behind, after, the other pieces

blocks.note: a curse someone utters when irritated
to sand a surface is to polish it

annotation.surface: Someone irritated by people standing behind a Polish national anthem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polish national song' reads as an anthem; the capital P hides the plain verb polish.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: this is Noël Coward's comic song about the English going out in the midday sun.

entries.clue: Wish before dance ball (4,3)

blocks.note: to long for is to wish for
a hop is an informal dance

annotation.surface: Making a wish before going to a dance ball.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dance ball' paints a ballroom; the ball here is a delivery in cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket term: a long hop is a short-pitched ball that bounces high and is easy to hit.

entries.clue: A number one in Abba hit, health hazard! (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the number one goes in, inside, the song title

annotation.surface: An Abba chart-topper denounced as a danger to health.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads as a chart position that suits 'hit', but it is a word for the top.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: asbestos fibres cause lung disease, making it a notorious health hazard.

entries.clue: Familiar name, not so for burner (7)

indicatorNotes.not so: 'not so' means without SO, so those two letters are removed

blocks.note: the two letters taken off the front

annotation.surface: A nickname that isn't so familiar after all, given to someone who burns things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not so' reads as a denial, but it tells you to drop the letters SO.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a briquet, or briquette, is a block of compressed coal dust made for burning.

entries.clue: Still case incomplete after arrest of Romeo for murders (8)

indicatorNotes.incomplete: an incomplete word is missing its last letter
indicatorNotes.after arrest of: to arrest is to detain, so the shortened case holds R inside it

blocks.note: a chest is a box or case
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A detective's frustration: the murder case still unfinished after Romeo is arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: The police story makes 'case' a criminal case and 'arrest' a detention; here the case is a box, and it holds the letter inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to butcher people is to murder them brutally.

entries.clue: African line crossed by an Indian (7)

indicatorNotes.crossed by: the line is crossed by the other letters, which lie on either side of it

annotation.surface: An African border line that an Indian traveller crosses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indian' is a person from one particular Indian state, which is a common crossword trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: an Angolan is a person from Angola in southern Africa.

entries.clue: Filthy old measure (5)

blocks.note: a traditional count of twelve dozen, 144

annotation.surface: A dirty old unit of measurement.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense survives in wholesale trade, where goods were counted in dozens of dozens.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: disgusting, and a count of 144 items.

entries.clue: Birds I located in parts east of Idaho, finally (7)

indicatorNotes.located in: the I is located inside the parts
indicatorNotes.east of: in an across answer east is to the right, so the parts come after the letter from Idaho
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so take the last letter

annotation.surface: A birder reporting sightings in the region east of Idaho.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as regions of the country; it is theatrical roles.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: orioles are brightly coloured songbirds.

entries.clue: Old peacekeepers when safe go it alone: UN formed (6,2,7)

indicatorNotes.formed: to form something is to shape it, so the letters are shaped into a new order

annotation.surface: Old peacekeeping forces going solo once the UN was set up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is history in a nutshell: the older body was wound up when the United Nations was founded.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the League of Nations was the international body set up to keep the peace after the First World War.

entries.clue: Animal lugged by the lugholes? (4)

indicatorNotes.by the lugholes: lugholes is British slang for ears, so the word is taken in by ear, as it sounds

annotation.surface: An animal hauled along by its ears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lugholes' echoes 'lugged' and makes the ears sound like handles to drag by.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the toad is an amphibian.

entries.clue: Covert operation as cry heard from protesting vegan? (8)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is spoken, so the cry is taken by its sound

blocks.note: what a vegan might chant against meat

annotation.surface: A secret police operation posing as a vegan protest.
annotation.walkthrough: The vegan chant against beef sounds just like the police term for watching a building.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a stakeout is secret surveillance of a place, one kind of covert operation.

entries.clue: Openers depend on this critical call (3,4)

blocks.note: to ring is to call on the phone

annotation.surface: Batsmen whose innings hinges on one crucial umpiring decision.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen; here they are things that open locks, which literally hang from the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: keys are openers, and they depend, in the sense of hang, from this holder.

entries.clue: Republican has broken you — told you so! (5)

indicatorNotes.has broken: the Republican has broken into the other word, so it sits inside it

annotation.surface: A gloat after a Republican defeats you.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation of someone proved right, as in 'There! What did I say?'
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: said with satisfaction, the word means 'I told you so!'

entries.clue: Fiction at first avoided, reaches for novel — a classic perhaps? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.at first: at first points to the opening letter
indicatorNotes.avoided: an avoided letter is kept out, so it is removed from 'for'
indicatorNotes.novel: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the opening letter, which is the one to avoid

annotation.surface: Someone skipping fiction and reaching for a novel instead, perhaps a classic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'classic' both suggest books; the Classics are the five great British flat races, such as the Derby.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with 'perhaps' to show it: each of the five Classics is one kind of horse race.

entries.clue: Cast actor in a production designed for the outdoors? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the phrase describes the garment, a thing designed for the outdoors

indicatorNotes.Cast: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown about
indicatorNotes.production: a production makes something, so the letters are made into a new word

annotation.surface: Casting an actor in an open-air play.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre words 'cast' and 'production' look like context for 'actor', but both signal the rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description with a question mark: a waterproof coat is designed for wear outside.

entries.clue: The obligation is on me to drink — absolutely! (1,6,5)

blocks.note: the duty is mine: I ought to

annotation.surface: Someone who feels duty-bound to have a drink, and heartily agrees.
annotation.walkthrough: This is old British slang, a play on 'I should say so', used to mean certainly, often ironically.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional idiom: the British exclamation means 'I should think so!', that is, absolutely.

entries.clue: Musical setter? (9)

blocks.note: the stage show set in 1960s Baltimore
something that fixes a hairstyle in place

annotation.surface: A crossword setter with a musical bent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the usual word for a crossword compiler; here it is a product that sets a hairdo.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the title of a Broadway musical, and a spray that sets hair.

entries.clue: Woman turned hose around opening of dirty trough to clean animals (5-3)

indicatorNotes.turned: a turned word faces the other way, so the hose is read backwards
indicatorNotes.around: the reversed hose goes around the letter that follows
indicatorNotes.opening of: the opening of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A farmer's wife turning a hose on a filthy trough to wash livestock.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard picture is apt, but the hose is not sprayed: it is a word that gets flipped and wrapped round a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a sheep-dip is a bath of insecticide that sheep are plunged through to clean their fleece.

entries.clue: Fitting, with little to spare (4)

blocks.note: deserved and fair, as a fitting reward is
barely, by a narrow margin, as in catching a train with seconds left

annotation.surface: Clothes that fit, but only barely.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the two halves one idea, a snug fit; they are two separate meanings of one short word.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: fair or deserved, and only barely.

entries.clue: Tread on rogue in group, fantasist (5,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece on another sits directly above it, so the tread comes before the rogue
indicatorNotes.in: the pair goes in, inside, the group

annotation.surface: Stepping on a scoundrel in a gang of dreamers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tread on' looks like one phrasal verb, to step on; split it, and 'on' just places one piece above the next.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: a space cadet is someone with their head in the clouds, out of touch with reality.

entries.clue: Old capital governed, tough (7)

blocks.note: a goon is a hired thug, a tough

annotation.surface: A former capital ruled with a firm hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tough' looks like an adjective about the rule; it is a noun, a heavy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma until 2005.

entries.clue: One without scent bottles still (9)

indicatorNotes.bottles: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the word for scentless holds the one

blocks.note: with no nose, so unable to smell

annotation.surface: A person who cannot smell bottling a still, as if making spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' and 'still' conjure a distillery; 'still' is the adjective, quiet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: still means making no sound.

entries.clue: Each day appended to this month, preferably (7)

indicatorNotes.appended to: appended means added at the end, so the each and day letters follow the month

blocks.note: inst., instant, is old business-letter shorthand for this month

annotation.surface: A diary rule: add each day to this month's schedule, if you would.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces read in reverse of the clue order: the month comes first, then the other two are tacked on.
annotation.definitionFit: A close synonym: 'I'd have tea instead' means I'd preferably have tea.

entries.clue: Country in rift, about which unhappy (9)

indicatorNotes.about which: about means around, so the unhappy word goes around what came before

annotation.surface: A nation in the middle of an unhappy dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In rift' reads as a country divided; 'in' is literal letters, not a position.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Singapore is a city-state in Southeast Asia.

entries.clue: A boy from Bamako, for example, standing to welcome a priest (5,4)

indicatorNotes.standing: in a down answer, standing up means reading from the bottom
indicatorNotes.to welcome: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the phrase takes in the second A

blocks.note: Bamako is the capital of Mali, so its people are an example of those from Mali
the welcomed A, taken in after the country

annotation.surface: A Malian boy getting to his feet to greet a visiting cleric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For example' shows the boy stands for any lad from Mali; 'standing' flips the whole string upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Dalai Lama is the chief priest, or lama, of Tibetan Buddhism.

entries.clue: Many debts owed by policeman (7)

indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so the debts sit next to the policeman

blocks.note: an IOU is a note of a debt owed

annotation.surface: A policeman in trouble over lots of unpaid debts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Owed by' tells a story about a debt-ridden officer, but 'by' is just a positioning word.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: copious means plentiful, in large numbers.

entries.clue: Versatile — as cabaret? (3-7,3-7)

blocks.note: with every feature you could want
a cabaret show literally offers song and dance throughout

annotation.surface: A cabaret act praised for being able to do everything.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a cabaret really is full of performers vocalising and moving to music.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase describes something with every possible feature, like a gadget that does everything.

entries.clue: Brass, a pound on something irritating (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the pound comes before the irritant

blocks.note: L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

annotation.surface: Complaining that money, a pound here and there, is irritating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brass' is British slang for money, which fits the pound; here it means a brass instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the althorn is a valved brass instrument of the saxhorn family.

entries.clue: Illness confined to jail, men treatable (7)

indicatorNotes.confined to: something confined is locked inside, so the answer is locked inside the words that follow

blocks.note: all of jail but the J, all of men, and the T of treatable

annotation.surface: A prison doctor assures inmates their illness can be treated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Confined to jail' fits the prison story too well to look like an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an ailment is an illness, usually a minor one.

entries.clue: Choral work provided great piece of rock (6)

annotation.surface: A choir piece that turns out to be a great rock song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great piece of rock' seems to continue the music; it is geology.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a massif is a compact block of mountains, a great mass of rock.

entries.clue: Hence, day tricky (6)

blocks.note: THU is the calendar abbreviation for Thursday

annotation.surface: A remark that the day ahead will therefore be difficult.
annotation.walkthrough: Any day could do; only Thursday's short form fits the crossing letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: thusly, a jokey form of thus, can mean in this way and so, hence.

entries.clue: For example, the bit without intro (7)

indicatorNotes.without intro: a word without its intro has lost its introduction, its first letter

blocks.note: a particle is a tiny bit

annotation.surface: Cutting the introduction off a piece of writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The' is not filler: in grammar it is the definite one of its word class, so 'for example, the' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'the' is the definite article in English grammar.

entries.clue: Gentleman positioned horizontally for prayer? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the phrase describes the person, one there for prayer
annotation.surface: A man lying flat on the floor, perhaps prostrated in prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose definition: the man is someone you would go to for prayer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a chaplain is a clergyman attached to a school, hospital or regiment, who leads prayers.

entries.clue: Tea cups in — this material? (5)

indicatorNotes.cups: to cup something is to hold it in curved hands, so the tea holds IN inside itself

blocks.note: cha is British slang for tea

annotation.surface: Asking what tea cups are made of.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cups' is the verb, holding a word, while the surface makes it the noun; the whole also asks what cups are made of.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: fine porcelain is the material tea cups are traditionally made of.

entries.clue: Put lid on alcoholic drink (6)

blocks.note: to put a stop to something, as with a rumour

annotation.surface: Capping a bottle of spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put lid on' is not about bottles: it means to put the lid on a plan, to squash it.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to thwart or end something, and whisky from Scotland.

entries.clue: National reporter’s commitment (4)

indicatorNotes.reporter’s: a reporter speaks the news, so the word is taken as a reporter would say it

blocks.note: a tie is something that binds you, a commitment

annotation.surface: A national newspaper's reporter showing dedication.
annotation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here, a citizen of a country, not an adjective for the newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a person from Thailand is one country's national.

entries.clue: Sitcom mainly about impassive individual (5)

indicatorNotes.mainly: mainly means for the most part, so most of the word, minus its last letter
indicatorNotes.about: to turn about is to move around, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: the word without its last letter

annotation.surface: A situation comedy built around a deadpan character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', which suits the sitcom story; it is the rearranging signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stoic endures hardship without showing feeling.

entries.clue: Chapter in English constitutes poetic lines on page (7)

indicatorNotes.on: on means placed next to, so the page is joined to the pieces around it

annotation.surface: A chapter of an English book made up of verse on the page.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces are not assembled in clue order: the page letter slots in right after English.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an episode is one part, or chapter, of a longer story.

entries.clue: Dry your hands when muddied (9)

indicatorNotes.when muddied: muddied water is stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

annotation.surface: Advice to wipe your hands after getting them dirty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like an instruction to wipe your hands; it is the definition, an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: in chemistry, anhydrous means containing no water.

entries.clue: Overture OK having introduced girls to endless wine (7,4)

indicatorNotes.having introduced: to introduce something is to bring it in, so OK takes the girls and wine inside
indicatorNotes.endless: an endless word has had its end, its last letter, removed

annotation.surface: An overture approved because it brought some girls to an unlimited supply of wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The grid has no room for an apostrophe, so the title is entered without one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Fingal's Cave is Mendelssohn's concert overture, also called The Hebrides.

entries.clue: As shot, it tumbled into river, in other words (4,2,2,3)

indicatorNotes.tumbled: tumbled letters have fallen out of order and are rearranged
indicatorNotes.into: the mixed letters go into, inside, the river

blocks.note: the letters of these words rearranged
the Tay is a Scottish river

annotation.surface: Someone shot and falling into a river, explained another way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As shot' looks like a description of the victim, but those words are letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase introduces a restatement, just as 'in other words' does.
